name: Rolling Escape from Anaconda
summary: An Anaconda escape must first address the head-and-arm enclosure; a roll is conditional on an open neck space and does not automatically create Dead Orchard.
description: An Anaconda escape must first address the head-and-arm enclosure; a roll is conditional on an open neck space and does not automatically create Dead Orchard.
overview:
The defender is beneath a front-headlock attacker whose arm encloses the neck and one shoulder. A secured choke is a tap situation. Dead Orchard is a separate high guard, not the continuation of an Anaconda roll, and no blind rolling escape is guaranteed.

An arm passing beneath the neck toward the armpit signals the Anaconda enclosure. Preserve space between the shoulder and neck before the attacker closes the arm loop. Do not fight a secured loop by twisting the neck or planting the head against a roll.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Denis Kang — the Anaconda choke](https://www.grapplearts.com/the-anaconda-choke/); [Nathan Orchard — Dead Orchard, part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoiB1D2WJwE).

defender.name: Rolling Escape from Anaconda Defender
defender.description: Rolling Escape from Anaconda (defender): Contain the opponent's head and one arm while keeping a balanced base. Pass the choking arm beneath the neck and toward the far armpit, enclosing one shoulder.
defender.overview:
The defender is beneath a front-headlock attacker whose arm encloses the neck and one shoulder. A secured choke is a tap situation. Dead Orchard is a separate high guard, not the continuation of an Anaconda roll, and no blind rolling escape is guaranteed.

Contain the opponent's head and one arm while keeping a balanced base. Pass the choking arm beneath the neck and toward the far armpit, enclosing one shoulder. Join to the supporting arm without pulling the neck into a twist.

Use the taught shoulder-led angle only when both partners can roll safely; do not dive onto the neck. Bring the trapped shoulder toward the neck with gradual whole-body connection rather than a violent head pull. Open both arms immediately on a tap or any loss of normal responsiveness.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
key_principles: Establish front headlock: Contain the opponent's head and one arm while keeping a balanced base.
Thread under the neck: Pass the choking arm beneath the neck and toward the far armpit, enclosing one shoulder.
Connect the arm loop: Join to the supporting arm without pulling the neck into a twist.
Choose a controlled angle: Use the taught shoulder-led angle only when both partners can roll safely; do not dive onto the neck.
Close the shoulder gap: Bring the trapped shoulder toward the neck with gradual whole-body connection rather than a violent head pull.
Release the loop: Open both arms immediately on a tap or any loss of normal responsiveness.

flashcards.question: Anaconda rolling escape (holder): What does your initial arm enclosure contain?
flashcards.answer: This retained defender deck belongs to the front-headlock holder, whose Anaconda contains the head and one arm.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's head and one arm

plausible: Neck alone with both arms outside
The head and both opposing arms
trap: One upper arm with the head outside

flashcards.question: Anaconda rolling escape (holder): Where does the choking arm pass first?
flashcards.answer: Thread beneath the neck and toward the far armpit to enclose one shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: Under neck toward the far armpit

plausible: Through the armpit toward the neck
Over shoulder toward the upper back
trap: Under neck but outside the upper arm

flashcards.question: Anaconda rolling escape (holder): Where does the threading hand grip in the arm figure-four?
flashcards.answer: The threading hand grips the supporting arm's biceps to close the figure-four. Connect without twisting the opponent's neck; the drill can stop at the unloaded enclosure. Kesting emphasizes sufficient threading depth rather than a shallow fingertip contact.

plausible: Palms clasped before the shoulder
Supporting wrist beside the shoulder

flashcards.question: Anaconda rolling escape (holder): Where does your head belong during the taught controlled roll?
flashcards.answer: Kesting's account places the holder's head to the side of the body during the roll. Use the angle only with free, controlled movement and immediate release on a tap.

plausible: On the opponent's upper back
Above the back of their neck
